title: 北海道廃線路線図 — 北海道
creator: 苗穂工房 (naeboworks)
source_license_evidence_section: 廃線路線図データ(KMLファイル)のご利用案内
attribution: 北海道廃線路線図 © 2007–2026 苗穂工房 (naeboworks); mapped from GSI Japan aerial photographs (CC BY 4.0).
changes: Converted KML coordinates and metadata to GeoJSON.
Filtered out current, threatened and signal-only markers; retained explicit closed/converted markers.

Excluded four paths containing never-opened railway construction, five construction endpoints and one never-used bridge marker. The mixed Meiu path also contained an industrially operated section; that working corridor is represented separately by OSM w990215687, with museum evidence.
Trimmed never-opened continuations after Omu (Kohinnan line) and Koshikawa (Konpoku line) by cutting on the existing source polylines nearest the source station positions.
Excluded two mine-site rail paths whose closure was not established.
Assigned historical status/type and preserved source notes; no missing operation dates were inferred.
Station coordinates were not snapped or moved; no route connections were invented. Except for those two documented terminal cuts, source path coordinates were preserved.

supplemental_primary_status_evidence.purpose: Esashi municipal museum study distinguishes operated Bifuka–Niupu Biko railway from never-completed Niupu–Kitami-Esashi extension.
2026 municipal page reports continuing Kushiro coal mining; closure of mine-site tracks not established, so excluded.
Kushiro museum documents Taiheiyo Rinko railway transport ending March 2019 and closure June 2019; its former paths remain included.
Shari municipal museum documents Koshikawa bridge as never used; bridge point and continuation after Koshikawa station excluded.

limits: Not a complete historical railway inventory; it inherits the creator's mapped coverage.
Approximate routes reconstructed from historical aerial imagery and creator site visits; no positional accuracy guarantee.
Different dates and realignments coexist; this is an all-era layer, not a synchronized historical snapshot.
Station markers are former sites, boarding places and some signal/freight sites; they are not a count of unique public passenger stations.
Naeboworks data remains a separate CC BY 4.0 source; it is not represented as OSM data or relicensed as ODbL/GPL.
Source descriptions link Wikipedia, but no prose from linked articles was imported.
